title: Wave 2: Rust ref precision — extract method-call names
description: walk_refs_recursive collects only identifier/type_identifier; field_identifier (method name in x.method()) is never extracted, and receiver-position identifiers are classified FieldAccess and skipped by the resolver. Result: sutra_impact/refs/calls/dead systematically wrong for idiomatic Rust (Db::upsert_file → 0 callers); manufactured a 100% false-positive dead-code list in this review. Finding: rust-refs-miss-method-calls (HIGH). Locations: src/parser/rust.rs:603-630, src/resolver.rs:46-57.

acceptance_criteria.text: field_identifier nodes inside call_expression extracted as Call-context refs
receiver-position identifiers (e.g. SKIP_DIRS.contains(...)) produce usable refs
full reparse of sutra workspace forced after fix
sutra_impact(Db::upsert_file) reports real callers (acceptance test from review)
sutra_dead false-positive rate collapses: previously-flagged live symbols (rules.rs methods, db/graph.rs, similarity machinery) no longer reported dead

execution_record:
Parser changes in src/parser/rust.rs:
1. walk_refs_recursive: added second extraction arm for field_identifier nodes in method-call position (parent=field_expression, grandparent=call_expression), tagged as RefContextKind::Call
2. classify_ref_context: changed field_expression arm to only classify field_identifier as FieldAccess — receiver identifiers now fall through to Other and get resolved normally
3. Added is_method_call_name helper
4. 5 new unit tests: method_call_extracts_call_ref, receiver_not_field_access, chained_method_calls, plain_field_access_no_method_ref, self_method_call

Verification after rebuild + full reparse (content hashes cleared):
- Db::upsert_file: 0 → 163 callers
- Db::insert_ref: 0 → 38 callers
- sutra_dead: 45 items, none from rules.rs/db/graph.rs/similarity (previously ~100% false-positive)
- All 291+ tests pass, clippy clean

edges.note: verifying the ref fix against a corrupted index proves nothing — heal duplicates first
guard fix should be verified against trustworthy refs
